fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. John the Baptist is on the list the disciples give Jesus. He's the one who came baptizing and preaching in the wilderness (Mark 1:4). Elijah and one of the prophets are the other guesses people had. So some people were naming John when they talked about who Jesus was.

Peter did take Him aside, so I get the guess. But Jesus doesn't agree with him. He turns, looks at His disciples and rebukes Peter, calling him Satan and saying Peter isn't thinking about the things of God but the things of men. So the answer is no, friend.

Right. Jesus says, “If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation…” Then He says the Son of Man will also be ashamed of that person when He comes in His Father's glory with the holy angels. It's a serious line, so I'll keep my jokes in the oven.
